target_constraint: Must minimize polyethylene wear under 10+ million flexion cycles
observed_phenomenon: Tibial insert wear causing implant loosening and pain
mechanism: Heat treatment of CoCrMo bearing surfaces alters microstructure to improve wear resistance, reducing abrasive damage to the polyethylene counterface.
intervention: Apply an optimized heat treatment (as described in the evidence) to the polished femoral component of the knee implant to produce a more wear-resistant CoCrMo microstructure, thereby reducing third-body abrasive wear of the highly cross-linked polyethylene tibial insert under 10+ million flexion cycles.
expected_effect: Reduced polyethylene wear rate and extended implant longevity by minimizing abrasive damage from the femoral bearing surface, while maintaining corrosion resistance.
falsification_test: Conduct pin-on-disk tribometer wear testing for 10 million cycles in bovine serum, comparing heat-treated CoCrMo pins against untreated CoCrMo pins articulating against highly cross-linked polyethylene disks; measure polyethylene wear volume and surface roughness. If heat-treated CoCrMo does not show significantly lower polyethylene wear than untreated CoCrMo, the intervention is falsified.
source_spans: "This research examines various heat treatments of CoCrMo and their resulting microstructure and properties for hip and knee implant bearing surfaces. After heat treatment, wear tests were performed using a pin on disk tribometer for two million cycles, and corrosion testing was performed using a 3-electrode cell potentiostat in bovine serum to simulate condit"
